items.snippet_en: AFP reported on March 12, 2020, that claims circulating on Facebook about warm water with lemon preventing coronavirus are false. Experts confirmed there's no proof of its effectiveness, and good hygiene is the best way to stay healthy.
Samayam Tamil, on May 26, 2021, addressed the misconception that lemon and hot water can kill the coronavirus, stating it is completely false and lacks scientific evidence.

FactCheck.org, on April 2, 2020, debunked a social media post claiming a blend of sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice would "eliminate" the novel coronavirus, emphasizing that there is no specific medicine recommended to prevent or treat COVID-19.
VOA, on May 18, 2021, also highlighted that lemon juice will not cure COVID-19, categorizing such claims as "fake news."
While lemons are rich in Vitamin C and can boost the immune system, which is generally beneficial for health, this does not mean they can destroy the coronavirus.
